results.actual: Non-last SUPER_ADMIN delete, disable and demote returned 200; all three operations against the last active SUPER_ADMIN returned 409 LAST_ACTIVE_SUPER_ADMIN.
The operator list contained only the two active Operations users; direct lookup of the Sales user returned 404.
Same-department Media read returned 200, peer delete returned 403, creator delete returned 200 and cross-department read was denied.
Same-department Layout read returned 200, peer update returned 403, creator update returned 200 and cross-department read was denied.
Same-department Presentation read and administrator read returned 200; peer mutation returned 403 and cross-department read was denied.
Same-department Schedule read/update and administrator read returned 200; cross-department read was denied.
ADMIN-created Media/Layout/Presentation/Schedule were ORGANIZATION and department-readable; SUPER_ADMIN-created equivalents were RESTRICTED and denied.
A custom role with an arbitrary name created all four content types and used its granted mutations; a missing User.read grant returned 403.
Delegate direct allowed Screen returned 201; other Screen, Group and Global returned 403; ADMIN Group and SUPER_ADMIN Global returned 201.
Delegate cleared its allowed Screen emergency with 200; clearing an unassigned Screen emergency returned 403 and the emergency remained active.
Three general Requests probes returned 404 while Schedule Requests list returned 200.
Old sessions returned 401 immediately after disable, password reset and role-permission removal; the new password logged in successfully.
For one Screen in two Groups, priority 90 won over 10; Group metadata edit and an assignment update omitting priority retained 90 and the correct winner.
After clearing Screen/Group, aspect and global defaults, the live API returned source NONE, media_id null and media null instead of a standard company image.
